 Netflix Seals Fast & Furious Fate Ahead of Long-Awaited Sequel
 Paul Walker in The Fast and the Furious Image via Universal/courtesy Everett Collection 
 By  
 Anthony Nash 
 Published Oct 19, 2026, 7:00 PM EDT 
 Anthony Nash has been writing about all things entertainment for over a decade. When he’s not writing about games or movies, he’s usually playing or watching them. You can find him on social media talking movies, sports, and all things games.

 Fast & Furious is one of the most popular franchises of all time. For a long time, most of those films have been able to be watched under one roof, but soon, the movies are being split up and will be a bit tougher to watch ahead of the long-awaited 11th entry.
 According to Netflix , most of the mainline Fast & Furious franchise is set to leave the streaming platform at the end of the month. This includes the first, third, fourth, fifth, sixth, and seventh movies in the franchise. While most of the franchise will be gone, there will still be a handful of films to watch.
 2 Fast 2 Furious , the second entry in the series, as well as 2017's The Fate of the Furious , the eighth movie in the franchise, recently joined the streaming platform this month and will be available for the foreseeable future.
 The Fast & Furious Franchise Will Have Various Streaming Homes
 It's unclear where the new movies will be moving once they leave Netflix on Nov. 1. Right now, the latest two installments, 2021's F9 and 2023's Fast X , are available to watch on Peacock, as Universal owns the rights to the franchise, so it's likely the films are heading back to Peacock. The 2019 spin-off Hobbs & Shaw , which stars Dwayne Johnson and Jason Statham, is available to stream on Hulu, adding yet another platform for the franchise.
 In 2001, the Fast & Furious franchise was about illegal street racing and a heist crew using their modified cars to steal electronic goods and sell them to keep up their racing habits. For about four films, the story followed the group, led by Vin Diesel's Dominic Toretto, until the franchise opened up into the wider action genre.
 Since 2011's Fast Five , the series has largely taken place in the world of heist and espionage genres, with the group sometimes finding themselves wrapped up in adventures that include battling cyberterrorists, saving the world, and much more. Alongside Diesel, Fast & Furious has featured the late Paul Walker, Sung Kang, Michelle Rodriguez, Tyrese Gibson, Chris "Ludacris" Bridges, Jordana Brewster, and more, most of whom are still part of the current films.
 Later movies have added megastars like Dwayne Johnson, Jason Statham, Helen Mirren, John Cena , Nathalie Emmanuel, Kurt Russell, Charlize Theron, and more to the cast. Fast & Furious is extremely successful, having grossed over $7.3 billion across its 11 total movies. This makes it the eighth-highest-grossing franchise in history, just behind X-Men , James Bond , Avengers , Harry Potter , and more.
 What Do We Know About the Future of the Fast & Furious Franchise?
 Dominic Toretto (Vin Diesel) shields Isabel Neves (Daniela Melchior) in Fast X Image via Universal/Everett Collection 
 The latest film in the Fast & Furious series came out in 2023, with Fast X . It followed the story of Dominic Toretto trying to protect his family against the mysterious Dante Reyes (played by Jason Momoa), who seeks to get revenge for his father's death in Fast Five .
 With a budget of a whopping $378.8 million, Fast X is the sixth-most expensive movie ever made. Despite earning over $714 million at the box office, it largely underperformed, even though it was the fifth-highest-grossing release of 2023. At the time of the tenth installment's release, Diesel announced that two sequel films were in the works, depending on how Fast X performed.
 Since then, things have changed. After Fast X underperformed, reports suggested that the next could be the final in the Fast & Furious franchise , which Diesel confirmed in 2024. Titled Fast Forever , little is known about the plot, but Diesel said the final entry would return to its street racing roots and also feature Brian O'Connor, Walker's character, who was last seen in 2015's Furious 7 following the actor's tragic death.
 Louis Leterrier, who directed the tenth entry, is rumored to return for Fast Forever , although there's been no official confirmation. Diesel said earlier this year that the screenplay was completed by Michael Lesslie, and that filming is set to begin sometime in December.
 The Fast & Furious franchise's first eight films are currently available to watch on Netflix until Nov. 1, with 2 Fast 2 Furious and The Fate of the Furious staying on the platform.
